title: UNI GS Christy Hoffman to speak at Paris Summit Against International Oligarchy - UNI Global Union
content:
20.11.26 UNI General Secretary Christy Hoffman will speak at the first Paris Summit Against International Oligarchy on Saturday 21 November 2026 at the Théâtre de la Concorde. The summit was initiated by the International Tax Observatory, led by economist Gabriel Zucman. It brings together economists, researchers, politicians, journalists, trade unionists and activists to debate how to respond to extreme wealth and the concentration of economic, media and technological power. Hoffman will take part in the opening debate, “IA : pour une propriété universelle des savoirs” (AI: for universal ownership of knowledge), at 11.30 a.m. She will be joined by sociologist Isabelle Ferreras of the University of Louvain and economist Cecilia Rikap of University College London, along with a keynote address by Nobel Prize-winning economist Esther Duflo. The panel will ask who owns the knowledge that AI draws on, how the value it generates should be shared and how to stop the technology from concentrating power even further. Hoffman will argue that much of that knowledge comes from workers, whose calls and keystrokes are being recorded to train AI systems, and that they need a say in how it is used and their fair share of what it earns. “When I started work, I could not have imagined how much more power billionaires would accumulate over the following decades, and AI is now accelerating that concentration. We cannot afford a failure of imagination now, because this power is becoming more entrenched by the day. The answer must be as global as the problem, and a critical part of it is stronger unions. Workers must have real power over how companies are run, and the public must have real control over the systems we all depend on. There should be no ceiling on how just and democratic our economies can become. I’m coming to Paris to help widen what our movement believes is possible.” Other speakers at the anti-oligarchy summit include Nobel laureates Paul Krugman, Joseph Stiglitz and Duflo as well as labour leaders such as SEIU-UHW President Dave Regan and the CGT General Secretary Sophie Binet. The day’s debates draw on a manifesto signed by around 100 intellectuals and published on the eve of the summit. title: Goldman Sachs (GS) Plunge 8% to Near $801 as Hot Inflation and Jobs Data Rattle Rate Outlook - FXLeaders
content: Shares of The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE: GS) tumbled sharply on Friday, plunging roughly 8% to trade near $801 per share. The drop marks the latest leg of a broader selloff that has erased nearly 30% from the Wall Street giant’s 52-week high of $1,154, pushing the stock deep into bear market territory and putting the psychological $800 threshold squarely in traders’ sights. Despite reporting record year-to-date revenue, strong third-quarter earnings, and securing lucrative lead underwriting roles on blockbuster deals—including Anthropic’s historic IPO and a $44 billion SpaceX financing package—Goldman Sachs has been caught in a perfect storm of macroeconomic headwinds and market-wide risk aversion. Broad Market & AI Rout: Wall Street is enduring its worst losing streak since 2020. A sharp pullback in artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks—compounded by regulatory concerns following the U.S. midterm elections and executive upheaval at Nvidia—has sent the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) surging above 31. As a heavyweight component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average, Goldman Sachs has been among the hardest-hit blue-chip stocks as institutional investors de-risk portfolios. Hawkish Federal Reserve Expectations: Hotter-than-expected October inflation and jobs data have forced markets to reprice interest rate expectations. With traders now anticipating potential rate hikes from the Federal Reserve by mid-2027, fears of tighter financial conditions have dampened sentiment across major banking stocks. Slowing Growth & Dealmaking Outlook: Investors are looking past Goldman’s strong 2026 earnings and pricing in a cooler 2027. Goldman Sachs’ own research team recently warned that global GDP growth in 2027 is “tilted to the downside” and projected that corporate earnings growth will decelerate significantly from 2026’s pace. A slower dealmaking and IPO pipeline directly threatens the investment banking fees that fueled Goldman’s earlier rally. Technical Breakdown: From a chart perspective, Friday’s drop pushed GS decisively below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. Market technicians note that persistent selling pressure has broken key support levels, with some analysts eyeing the $750 to $783 zone as the next major technical floor if $800 fails to hold. On the New York Stock Exchange, Goldman Sachs—alongside Nvidia acted as the primary drag on the Dow Jones Industrial Average during Friday’s session. While value-oriented analysts point out that Goldman’s underlying fundamentals and capital-markets dominance remain intact, near-term momentum remains firmly with sellers until broader equity volatility subsides

title: Climate action plan: GCC to extend sponge parks to all parks, playgrounds: Sameeran - DT Next
content: CHENNAI: The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) will extend its Sponge Park initiative to all parks and playgrounds across the city as part of its efforts to strengthen climate resilience, Corporation Commissioner GS Sameeran said on Friday. Speaking at a conference on Climate Responsive Urban Planning organised by C40, a collective promoting global climate action through cities, here, Sameeran said that the civic body would work with various government agencies to address the city's climate challenges through coordinated planning. “The GCC will work closely with the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA), Chennai Metro Rail Ltd (CMRL), Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC), Chennai Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority (CUMTA), electricity board and Revenue department. The energy and water requirements of urban data centres will also be incorporated into the city’s climate action plan,” he explained. The Sponge Park initiative, launched by the Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay under the Blue-Green Chennai policy, would be expanded across the city. “The GCC is also developing a 200-km pedestrian network, while MTC buses are being modernised,” he added, and cited the Vyasarpadi Climate Action Plan prepared by students and youth from the neighbourhood. “There’s an urgent need to link climate change discussions with people’s livelihood concerns. These kids had studied the impact of Cyclone Michaung in 2023 on the livelihoods of auto drivers and formulated a local action plan. Similar neighbourhood-level groups should be formed across Chennai.” He emphasised that the GCC was committed to transforming Chennai into a climate-resilient city with the guidance of C40 Cities. The conference marked the 10th anniversary of the partnership between Chennai and C40 Cities and the 20th anniversary of the global climate leadership network. Sameeran released two publications, Climate Action Guide for Urban Planners in India and Clean Air Zone Roadmap for Indian Cities. C40 Cities executive director Mark Watts, regional director (South and West Asia) Naim Keruwala, ITDP India MD Aswathy Dilip, CEPT University’s programme head (MUP) Rutul Joshi, Energiva senior portfolio manager Venkat Jayagopi and CMDA chief planner P Gajendra participated in the conference. title: Lewis Hamilton Says He Flew an F-16 at 9.5 Gs and Texted Tom Cruise About Top Gun 3 - MotorBiscuit
content: Lewis Hamilton has been swapping the cockpit of a Ferrari for that of a fighter jet. The seven-time world champion told a Las Vegas crowd he had just flown an F-16, and that the flight pulled 9.5 Gs, or nine and a half times the normal pull of gravity on his body. It is the kind of force that tests even a trained athlete. He shared the story at a fan forum ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix while answering questions about life after racing, footage of which was shared by praveenrandev on Instagram.  Hamilton started by saying that he was working on the second F1 movie. On the jet, he said: “I just went up in a fighter jet, and I texted Tom [Cruise], I’m ready for Top Gun 3. I was like, ‘I’ve got to be involved.'” “I definitely could do it. I flew the F16. 9.5 Gs, baby,” he added. The jet ride gave Hamilton an idea. He and Cruise have been friends for more than a decade, ever since Cruise invited him to visit the set of Edge of Tomorrow. It is an old ambition. Hamilton has said he turned down a fighter-pilot role in Top Gun: Maverick because of his F1 commitments, and recalled that he once told Cruise, “I will even be a janitor.” He has also said of the third film: “I will miss a race for it.” Paramount has since announced that Top Gun 3 is in development with Cruise and producer Jerry Bruckheimer, so his timing looks better now. Hamilton was a producer on the first F1 movie, which starred Brad Pitt as fictional driver Sonny Hayes, and he also appeared in it as himself. The project has some official backing. Producer Jerry Bruckheimer told the BBC: “We’re working on a sequel.” Apple, which released the original, has also been reported as involved in the follow-up, and the first film earned more than $630 million worldwide. Even so, Bruckheimer gave no release date and did not confirm whether Pitt will return. For now, both projects are a waiting game. The F1 sequel has no release date or confirmed cast, and Top Gun 3 has yet to say whether it has a seat for a Formula 1 champion. Still, a driver who can take 9.5 Gs in a fighter jet, text Hollywood’s biggest action star, and help shape the next racing blockbuster is clearly planning for life beyond the pit lane. If either film lands the way Hamilton likely hopes, his next big appearance may be on the screen rather than the grid. Your email address will not be published. title: Peterborough theatre history brought to life in free exhibition - Peterborough Matters
content:
David G-S as Fairy Godmother (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) David G-S as Fairy Godmother (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) A new exhibition is shining a spotlight on centuries of theatre history in Peterborough. Life’s a Stage, opening at Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery on 21 November 2026, explores the city’s theatrical heritage from the late 1700s to the present day. The exhibition runs until February 20, 2027, and features playbills, archive materials, and memorabilia from venues including the long-lost Theatre Royal, Hippodrome, and Embassy Theatre, as well as modern stages like The Crescent, The New Theatre, and the Key Theatre. Glenys Wass, heritage collections museum manager, said: "We are delighted to share this fascinating exhibition with our visitors. Cast of Cinderella (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) "We have enjoyed working with current staff at Landmark Theatres and The Cresset to develop the exhibition, along with hearing memories shared by past employees to create this exhibition. "We hope people have as much fun visiting it as we did creating it." Visitors can learn about the families who managed the theatres, the performers who graced the stages, and the evolution of Peterborough’s theatrical scene. The exhibition also celebrates the city’s pantomime tradition, with props and costumes from past productions and a mini stage where guests can take part in the fun. Life's A Stage (Image: Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery) Famous names who once performed in Peterborough, including Vera Lynn, George Formby, and Laurel and Hardy—who visited in 1952—are featured in the displays. To mark the opening, the museum will be welcoming a very special guest appearance from 'The Fairy Godmother,' Dame from this year’s Cinderella pantomime at Landmark Theatre’s New Theatre, who will be joining the launch alongside one of her naughty elves. Visitors will have the chance to meet the characters and pose for photos on Saturday, November 21, between 10am and 12 noon. The exhibition is free to attend at Peterborough Museum & Art Gallery. title: Ukrainian Company Unveils Ground Robot Control Station That Uses AI to Detect Drones - Оборонка
content: Ukrainian company TechUnity has unveiled AetherLink GS, a software-based control station for unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). The company shared the information with OBORONKA. The current version, AetherLink GS 1.2.0, has two artificial intelligence (AI) features: automatic road following and drone detection, including FPV drones. "Within a single interface, the operator can control the robot, view camera feeds, plan routes, and monitor the vehicle's status and connectivity," the company said. The Road Following feature analyzes camera footage, identifies the road, and automatically keeps the UGV moving along it. It works both day and night and can be configured for a specific platform. Meanwhile, the built-in drone detector analyzes video directly on the operator's computer without transmitting footage to a cloud service. Drone detection uses separate AI models for cameras with 1.7 mm and 2.8 mm lenses, operating in daytime and nighttime modes, as well as for a thermal imaging camera. According to TechUnity, both features are already being used in combat conditions. AetherLink GS supports simultaneous operation with multiple IP cameras and automatically discovers them on the network. The UGV's dimensions and movement trajectory can be overlaid on the video feed to make maneuvering easier. Screen recording and two-way audio communication are also supported. Starlink, LTE, and Mesh networks can be used to communicate with the UGV, with automatic switching between channels and load balancing. The operator can monitor connection status, data transmission latency, and the operation of the Starlink terminal. The software displays the UGV's position on a map, supports route planning, and allows the vehicle to follow a predefined track. The operator can also monitor the vehicle's operating mode, battery voltage, and battery discharge graph. Joysticks, gamepads, and gaming steering wheels can be used to control the UGV. The operator can also display video or a map on a separate monitor for a navigator and transfer the UGV's settings to another laptop. AetherLink GS currently works with TechUnity's JARVIS onboard computer, which is installed in UGVs from more than 25 manufacturers. The control station is provided free of charge for these systems. The company is also exploring the possibility of providing AetherLink GS to military personnel and UGV manufacturers using other onboard computers. As a reminder, in August, TechUnity unveiled its own cameras for unmanned ground vehicles and drones. title: Karol G's medical condition that causes weight gain: "People shouldn't care, I'm a singer" - MARCA
content: Karol G's medical condition that causes weight gain: "People shouldn't care, I'm a singer" The artist revealed it this way in her Netflix documentary titled "Tomorrow Was Very Beautiful" Singer Karol G is in one of the best moments of her professional career. Her songs and shows are a success, and projects keep multiplying in her career. One of them, without a doubt, is the appearance of her song "El Makinón" in the GTA VI video game. However, the artist has had moments in which she has not felt very well and has had health problems. Recently, she has had to postpone her concert in Mexico City due to a health issue that, according to some media outlets' speculation, could be the flu. However, in her documentary titled "Tomorrow Was Very Beautiful", she mentioned that she has another underlying health problem that "causes weight gain," an issue for which she has often been criticized, in her own words. The illness the artist suffers from, according to what she herself said, is insulin resistance, in addition to the hormonal imbalances she experiences. These two conditions work and interact in many ways but, one of them, is body weight. Insulin resistance promotes fat storage since, when cells respond poorly to insulin, the pancreas produces more to compensate. This excess, as Dr. Jorge Solano mentions, drives the body to store energy as fat and slows the use of this fuel. In addition, it is normal for those who suffer from this problem to feel an increase in hunger and cravings, due to fluctuations in glucose and insulin. On the other hand, it is normal for fat to accumulate in the abdominal and visceral area. All of this complicates weight loss and weight maintenance which, added to the hormonal imbalance, can present a fairly complex situation to deal with, especially when you have a great deal of public exposure. People shouldn't care how much weight, because I'm a singer, I'm not a model Aesthetic pressure is one of the issues women have to deal with in almost every area of their lives. One of those areas is the music industry. In that regard, many artists feel that there is a double standard when it comes to what is demanded of a man and a woman who have the same profession. Almost no man feels the scrutiny that women are subjected to in the artistic sphere. Additionally, in many cases, they feel they suffer from ageism and that natural aging penalizes women, as many women have mentioned in interviews. On the other hand, the pressure not only comes from outside, but in many cases, it is also exerted from "home". The important thing is to understand that we should not comment on other people's bodies without knowing the context, reason, or cause of a physical change. title: Chennai: Functional RWH systems now must for completion certificate - The New Indian Express
content: CHENNAI: Completion certificates for buildings in the city will be issued only after officials verify that their rainwater harvesting structures are functional, and not merely present, Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G S Sameeran said on Thursday. He was speaking on the sidelines of a stakeholder meeting by civic body with the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI), the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (CMWSSB), resident welfare associations and NGOs, to promote rainwater harvesting as part of the ‘Thuli’ people’s movement. According to a CMWSSB survey of 10 lakh properties, only six lakh had functional rainwater harvesting structures. The corporation aims to raise the number to 13-14 lakh buildings, covering at least 70% of the 17 lakh assessed properties in the city, wherever feasible, particularly in larger buildings. Sameeran said a government order (G.O. 193) issued by the municipal administration and water supply department on January 2 lays down schematic diagrams and guidelines on construction of rainwater harvesting structures based on soil types. Copies of the order will be distributed to RWAs, and residents will be trained in maintaining and repairing the structures, he said. Chennai requires 1,246 million litres per day (MLD) of water, of which around 80% comes from reservoirs such as Poondi, Puzhal and Chembarambakkam, around 12% from desalination plants and around 6% from groundwater, he said. The groundwater level was recorded at 5.6 m above the aquifer in 2026 against 7.9 m during previous years of heavy rainfall, he said. Despite receiving 612 mm of rainfall against the city’s annual requirement of 850 mm, reservoir storage remains low at an average of 41% against the usual level of around 60%, and the corporation is pinning hopes on the rain between November 23 and 26 to replenish them. Asked about the poor maintenance of rainwater harvesting structures, Sameeran said the GCC had created such facilities in 1,858 buildings, 1,013 parks, 87 major playgrounds and along 30,000 stormwater drains covering 3,000 km, but some had been damaged over time. On the structures developed using German technology at the wells of the Vadapalani and Chitrakulam temples, which were later left unattended, he said there were two types of sponge parks, and the one using eco-blocks with a honeycomb-like structure may not be suitable everywhere since they are made of plastic. The corporation is also rejuvenating 245 ponds and plans to develop sponge parks using the natural gradients of the land at locations such as playgrounds. title: Princeton neuroscience Ph.D. student detained by ICE - The Daily Princetonian
content: Eva Yi Xie GS, a third-year Ph.D. student in neuroscience, has been detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement at an airport near Washington, D.C. She is believed to be held in a detention center in Chantilly, Va. Xie is the first known Princeton student to be reported to be detained by ICE. “The University has arranged for legal counsel to represent the student,” University spokesperson Michael Hotchkiss wrote in a statement to The Daily Princetonian Thursday night. The Society for Neuroscience annual conference was held in Washington, D.C., from Saturday through Wednesday. Xie presented a poster at the conference on Wednesday titled “Entorhinal grid-like coding generalizes to jointly organize physical and cognitive dimensions.” Xie is a member of the Brody Lab. She is advised by neuroscience professor Carlos Brody and coadvised by neuroscience professor Nathaniel Daw and computer science professor Benjamin Eysenbach. “It seems wildly unfair,” Brody wrote in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ “Eva is a brilliant law-abiding student and wonderful person who has many talents to contribute to the United States. Detaining her, with the intent of deporting her, makes no sense whatsoever. It is cruel, and it is our country shooting itself in the foot.” Dean of the Graduate School Rodney Priestley emailed graduate students in the Princeton Neuroscience Institute about the incident at 11:01 p.m. Thursday evening. “We hope she is able to soon resume her studies at Princeton,” the email, obtained by The Daily Princetonian, read. “Please be assured that we will stay in close contact with the student’s family, her legal team, and her PNI colleagues as this situation is resolved.” Wynne Stagnaro GS, a fellow PNI graduate student in the Brody Lab, shared specifics of the incident in a message on the Graduate Student Government Slack. According to Stagnaro, Xie sent a “call for help” to her lab mates via Slack Thursday afternoon. She told the ‘Prince’ on Friday morning that the lab mates have been able to make contact with Xie. “Eva is a brilliant computational and experimental systems neuroscientist. She is also a valued colleague, mentor, and friend, and we are privileged that she chose our lab for her thesis research,” Stagnaro wrote in her message. “She went to a conference to present her work, and now she’s in a detention center. She should be home.” An X post from the Brody Lab shared similar sentiments. Stagnaro shared that members of the Brody Lab have been in touch with the office of Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., other elected officials, and members of the media. Stagnaro did not add anything beyond the Slack post in a statement to the ‘Prince.’ Xie is researching the “neural basis of decision-making.” She emigrated from China to the U.S. in 2016. She graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2024 with double majors in computer science and mathematics and a concentration in economics. She has interned with Meta, Microsoft AI, and IBM Research, among others. At MIT, Xie was one of three undergraduates elected to the Presidential Advisory Cabinet for Institute President Sally Kornbluth and chaired the MIT Judicial Review Board. She is now on the Policy Subcommittee of the Princeton Graduate Student Committee on the Graduate School. Xie previously organized a workshop called “Data on the Brain & Mind” for the 2025 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems. She is currently co-organizing the Annual Conference on Cognitive Computational Neuroscience for 2027 in Edinburgh, Scotland. Eysenbach and Daw could not immediately be reached for comment. ICE did not respond to multiple requests for comment. title: US Stocks Are Predicted to Extend Their Historic Rally as Gains Moderate - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The S&P 500 has generated triple-digit returns since the start of the bull market four years ago. While US stocks are forecast to climb higher in 2027, Goldman Sachs Research expects US stock returns to moderate as earnings growth slows. What is Goldman Sachs Research’s outlook for S&P 500 gains in 2027? The S&P 500 is predicted to generate a total return of 18% through the end of 2027 (as of November 17), writes Ben Snider, chief US equity strategist, in the team’s report. Earnings are expected to grow by a robust 11% in 2027, or 18% excluding mega-cap tech “other income” from private investment stakes. However, that is a step down from the roughly 30% growth rate this year, and growth will likely slow further in 2028. “Positive but decelerating growth has historically been associated with positive but moderating S&P 500 returns as well as rotations within the equity market,” Snider writes. In these environments, returns are typically driven by earnings growth as valuation multiples decline. US stocks are on pace in 2026 for a fourth-straight year of gains, and the S&P 500 has returned 120% since late 2022. This four-year bull market return ranks as the strongest in the last 50 years outside of the dot-com bubble and the recoveries following recessions, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “AI investment has driven a surge in S&P 500 earnings in 2026, but that tailwind should begin to fade in 2027,” Snider writes. Capital expenditures in artificial intelligence (AI) have produced about half of the S&P 500’s growth in earnings per share this year. That impulse will likely be smaller in 2027 as the growth rate of capex slows and depreciation expenses build, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Earnings growth is also expected to slow modestly in 2027 for companies outside of AI infrastructure. Even so, Snider expects earnings, rather than valuations, to continue to drive equity returns in 2027. He says elevated interest rates, decelerating earnings growth, and AI-driven uncertainty should prevent broad expansion in multiples, such as price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios, in 2027. “The biggest downside risk to equities in 2027 is a deterioration in the earnings outlook for 2028,” Snider writes. AI investment growth will likely remain robust in 2027, as will its contribution to S&P 500 earnings. However, the market is forward looking, and that theme could play out in a broad range of ways in 2028. In addition to uncertainty around AI investment spending in 2028, the potential for rising semiconductor supply threatens profit margins and earnings, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Our strategists estimate that each $50 billion of AI capex, or 1 percentage point change in semiconductor profit margins, in 2028 would shift S&P 500 earnings-per-share (EPS) growth by about 1 percentage point. If consensus S&P 500 EPS estimates fell back to the 30-year trend and the P/E ratio fell to the 30-year average of 17x, the S&P 500 would decline by roughly 25% to a level of approximately 5,600. In addition, S&P earnings growth and recent stock returns have been highly concentrated in a handful of stocks. As the earnings growth from the AI investment cycle fades, the key question is whether another sufficiently large source of earnings strength will emerge to sustain index-level profits, Snider writes. Some of the dynamics during the late stages of other bull markets—such as Federal Reserve rate hikes—are taking place today. “One striking contrast with past overextended bull markets is the lack of speculative mania in today’s market,” Snider notes. He points out that recent equity returns have generally tracked near-term earnings outlooks. While active fund managers faced a difficult backdrop in much of 2026, Snider says earnings-driven returns, elevated dispersion, and improving equity market breadth bode well for stock pickers heading into the new year. What themes are expected to drive US stocks in 2027? As AI capex decelerates, Snider expects investors to shift their focus to “the next earnings beneficiaries of the AI boom.” For example, cloud-operating hyperscalers have increasingly shown signs of monetization of their AI investments. Another theme in 2027 may reflect the surge in corporate borrowing that has taken place to fund AI investment. Strong capex has come in part at the expense of buybacks, according to Goldman Sachs Research. That may create opportunities in “buyback aristocrats”—stocks with strong free cash flow generation and a commitment to returning cash to shareholders. During the past few decades, periods of slowing earnings and economic growth have favored stocks with price momentum, upward earnings revisions, and "quality" attributes such as low volatility and strong balance sheets, Snider writes. He says the information technology and healthcare sectors have a history of outperformance in these situations. Investors may also benefit from diversifying into defensive stocks, such as consumer staples companies, that tend to deliver stable profits even when the economy slows, according to Snider. “Although our base case is for continued earnings growth and equity market appreciation, the downside risks associated with extended earnings and valuations argue for diversifying portfolios with select defensives,” he writes. title: BMW R 12 G/S Launched In India At Rs 25.40 Lakh - DriveSpark
content: The BMW R 12 G/S has been launched in India at an introductory ex-showroom price of Rs 25.40 lakh. It is sold only in the Pro variant as a completely built-up unit, with deliveries starting immediately. The design of the BMW R 12 G/S draws from the R 80 G/S, which entered production in 1980. The R 12 G/S pairs a 1,170cc boxer engine and shaft drive with an enduro-focused chassis, long-travel suspension and cross-spoke wheels. The air- and oil-cooled 1,170cc boxer twin engine of the BMW R 12 G/S makes 109hp at 7,000rpm and 115Nm at 6,500rpm. The engine's bore and stroke measure 101mm and 73mm, and it sends power to the rear wheel through a shaft drive setup. The exhaust exits on the left, ending in a high-mounted rear silencer. A tubular steel spaceframe underpins the motorcycle, with a repositioned steering head and a bolted-on rear frame. Up front are fully adjustable 45mm upside-down forks with 210mm of travel. The rear gets a Paralever swingarm and a fully adjustable monoshock with 200mm of travel. Braking uses twin 310mm front discs with two-piston floating calipers and a 265mm rear disc with a two-piston floating caliper. BMW Motorrad ABS Pro is standard and supports ABS braking while the motorcycle is leaned into a corner. The BMW R 12 G/S rides on a 21-inch cross-spoke front wheel, and the standard Enduro Package adds an 18-inch rear wheel with off-road tyres.The package also brings enduro footpegs, a larger engine guard, hand protection, a longer side stand and handlebar risers that raise the bars by 20mm.The BMW R 12 G/S weighs 229kg unladen, the seat height is 875mm and the fuel tank holds 15.5 litres. The BMW R 12 G/S sports a high-mounted front mudguard, a compact cockpit fairing, a slim fuel tank and a flat seat, with the boxer engine left exposed. India gets a single Light White paint scheme with a contrasting red seat and traditional graphics, like the original R 80 G/S. The compact LED headlamp has BMW's X-shaped lighting signature, and a round instrument display sits at the centre of the cockpit. A 12V power socket and two steel lashing points on the rear frame are also fitted. The Pro variant's Comfort Package, also standard, brings Shift Assistant Pro for clutchless gear changes, heated grips, cruise control, Hill Start Control and adaptive headlight functionality through Headlight Pro. Rain, Road and Enduro riding modes are standard, and the Enduro Package adds an Enduro Pro mode. Dynamic Traction Control and engine drag torque control (MSR) are standard as well, with the traction control switchable off for off-road riding. BMW Motorrad offers a three-year, unlimited-kilometre warranty on the R 12 G/S, extendable to the fourth and fifth years, along with 24x7 roadside assistance. It is worth noting that the R 12 G/S sits between the R 1300 GS and the R 1300 GS Adventure in India. BMW's boxer-twin engine is something of a legend, mostly thanks to the R 1200 GS and the GS Adventure. However, few people remember that it only got liquid cooling in 2013. Before this, it was air-and-oil cooled. Fans who miss the old engine can now buy it again. The off-roader also gets some modern upgrades. The R 12 G/S is powered by a  1,170cc boxer-twin engine, which produces 107.5bhp of power at 7,000rpm and 115Nm of torque at 6,500rpm. The engine is paired with a 6-speed gearbox. It has a 45mm upside-down fork with 210mm of travel, and it is fully adjustable. At the rear is the same fully adjustable paralever swingarm, with 200mm of travel. Like any bike with off-road roots, it runs on a 21-inch front wheel and an 18-inch rear wheel. Both use tubeless cross-spoke rims, which are handy for riders. Braking comes from twin 310mm front discs with two-piston callipers, and a 265mm rear disc with a two-piston calliper. Dual-channel, cornering-sensitive ABS is standard. These focused changes have made the bike larger. The kerb weight is 229kg, the wheelbase is 1,580 mm, and the seat is a towering 875mm high. This makes the R 12 G/S the heaviest, longest and tallest heritage bike yet from the German maker. There are four ride modes: Rain, Road, Enduro and Enduro Pro. Enduro Pro comes with the standard Enduro package. That package also adds the 18-inch rear wheel, enduro footrests, handlebar risers, a hand lever protector and a large engine guard. The risers lift the handlebar by 20mm. A standard Comfort package adds a two-way quickshifter, cruise control, hill-start assist and heated grips. The instrument cluster is analogue, with a small digital display at the bottom. The lighting is all LED, and the bike has an immobiliser and a keyless system. For charging your devices, however, it still has a 12V socket. The R 12 G/S comes in three colours abroad, but in India the enduro bike gets only one: Light White, in a single Pro version. title: GS Caltex beats Heungkuk Life to take sole lead after match delay - Chosunbiz
content: The match was chaotic, with play delayed for about 20 minutes after a medical emergency. GS Caltex defeated Heungkuk Life. GS Caltex beat Heungkuk Life 3-1 (25-19, 25-20, 18-25, 25-23) in a women's match in the 2026-27 HK Heungkuk Finance V-League at Samsan World Gymnasium in Incheon on the 19th. GS Caltex extended its winning streak to three games and moved to 4-1 with 12 points, tying IBK Industrial Bank of Korea and Korea Expressway Corporation (KEC), also 4-1, but took sole possession of first place on set differential. Heungkuk Life fell to its third straight loss, leaving it with six points (2-3). GS Caltex controlled the first two sets. In the first set, after trailing 13-12, Tanacha scored two aces and Silva followed with consecutive kills. Heungkuk Life's errors helped GS Caltex turn the match around and take an 18-13 lead. The second set was also closely contested, but at 17-17, Kwon Min-ji scored a block point. A net-touching error by the opposition, Kim Hyo-im's ace and a kill by Silva, followed by a string of opponent errors, helped GS Caltex seize control. But an unexpected situation arose in the third set, which swung in Heungkuk Life's favor. Early in the set, with Heungkuk Life leading 5-4, Justice scored on a quick attack and Jung Ho-young blocked a shot. Jung then added a quick attack and an ace to help build a 9-5 lead. Points from Kindelan, Justice and Jung, along with an ace by Kindelan, helped Heungkuk Life fend off GS Caltex's rally. With Heungkuk Life leading 19-14 in the third set, a spectator suffered a medical emergency in the first-floor stands near the press box. Play was stopped immediately, and medical staff came onto the court to treat the person. Emergency responders also arrived. Play was delayed for about 20 minutes while first aid was administered, and the person was then taken to a hospital. The match resumed at 8:43 p.m., and Heungkuk Life claimed the third set. GS Caltex ultimately rallied to win a tightly contested fourth set. After Yoo Seo-yeon's kill tied the score at 23-23, Kim Hyo-im scored an ace to give the team a 24-23 match point. Oh Se-yeon then finished the win with a kill. GS Caltex had four players score in double figures: Gisele Silva with 22 points, Choi Ga-eun and Tanacha with 12 each, and Kwon Min-ji with 11. Kindelan scored 35 points and Jung Ho-young added 14 for Heungkuk Life, but the team could not stop its losing streak at home. We use cookies to enhance your experience and analyze traffic. Benelli and GS Motos have taken another step forward in their industrial strategy in Mexico with the start of production of the Benelli TNT25N at GS Motos’ manufacturing plant in Toluca. The TNT25N production line operates at a rate of 34 units per hour, equivalent to approximately one motorcycle every 1.8 minutes. This pace is supported by a synchronized production process involving personnel, standardized procedures, and quality controls, with each station ensuring the precision and quality required for continuous production. The GS Motos manufacturing plant in Toluca has an annual production capacity of 1.2 million motorcycles. Since beginning operations in 2008, the facility has manufactured more than 10 million units. The start of TNT25N assembly further strengthens the role of the Toluca facility as a strategic manufacturing hub for GS Motos in Latin America. With the addition of the TNT25N, GS Motos is expanding its assembly capabilities in Mexico by incorporating another model into its multi-brand manufacturing operations. The move highlights the flexibility of its infrastructure and the expertise of its teams in producing motorcycles from different brands according to specific standards and requirements. title: BMW R 12 G/S Launched In India At Rs 25.40 Lakh - CarAndBike
content: BMW Motorrad has launched the retro-inspired R 12 G/S in India, priced at Rs 25.40 lakh (ex-showroom). Drawing inspiration from the iconic R 80 G/S of the 1980s, the R 12 G/S Enduro motorcycle is essentially a more off-road-ready version of the R 12 nine T. It gets a taller stance and long-travel suspension while continuing with the boxer-twin engine. In India, the motorcycle will be available in a single Pro variant and one colour scheme. Based on the same platform as the R 12 nine T, it has a distinctly different look, with a small headlight fairing, raised front fender and knuckle guards. It further gets a single-piece seat, a high-mounted silencer with its conical tailpipe. Power comes from the 1,170 cc air/oil-cooled, twin-cylinder boxer engine, which is carried over from the R 12 nineT. It produces 107 bhp at 7,000 rpm and 115 Nm at 6,500 rpm. It further gets three standard modes – Rain, Road and Enduro – while the more specialised Enduro Pro mode is available with the Enduro Package Pro. Dynamic Traction Control and engine drag torque control are standard. The R 12 G/S also gets keyless ignition, LED lighting and a round instrument cluster, with an adaptive headlight offered as an option. Suspension comprises fully adjustable upside-down forks with 210 mm of travel at the front and a monoshock with 200 mm of travel at the rear. Also Read: BMW F 450 GS Sport Variant Launched At Rs 5.90 Lakh The R 12 G/S rides on cross-spoke wheels, with a 21-inch front and 17-inch rear combination as standard. An 18-inch rear wheel can be specified as an option. Braking is handled by twin 310 mm discs at the front and a 265 mm disc at the rear. The motorcycle has a 15.5-litre fuel tank and tips the scales at 229 kg. Compared to the R 12 nine T on which it is based, the R 12 G/S commands a premium of Rs 1.90 lakh, but is an entirely different proposition.

It is available exclusively in the Pro variant for India with both the Comfort and Enduro packages included as standard. However, its 229kg unladen weight and 875mm seat height suggest that it will demand considerable experience when the going gets difficult. Drawing inspiration from the legendary R 80 G/S that established the foundations of the manufacturer's modern adventure motorcycle range, the new R 12 G/S features a high-mounted front mudguard, compact cockpit fairing, relatively slim fuel tank and a flat seat. Its exposed boxer engine and high-mounted exhaust further contribute to its traditional enduro appearance. The R 12 G/S concentrates on simplicity and a more purposeful design which makes soo desirable. For India, BMW is offering the motorcycle in a single Light White paint scheme complemented by a contrasting red seat and traditional graphics, like the original R 80 G/S. Its compact LED headlamp features BMW's distinctive X-shaped lighting signature and the relatively minimal bodywork keeps the motorcycle's mechanical components clearly visible. A centrally positioned circular instrument display reinforces the retro character. The 1,170cc air- and oil-cooled boxer-twin engine puts out 109bhp at 7,000rpm and 115Nm of torque at 6,500rpm. It comes with shaft final drive. BMW has developed a dedicated chassis arrangement for its off-road use. It features a tubular steel frame with a repositioned steering head and the rear subframe is bolted to the main structure. Front suspension has fully adjustable 45mm upside-down forks offering 210mm of wheel travel. Rear uses its Paralever swingarm with a fully adjustable monoshock offering 200mm of travel. The R 12 G/S uses a 21-inch front cross-spoke wheel. Enduro Package, included as standard in India, adds an 18-inch rear wheel with off-road tyres. Package also brings enduro footpegs, a larger engine guard, hand protection, a longer side stand and handlebar risers. The R 12 G/S also features a 15.5-litre fuel tank. India-spec R 12 G/S additionally receives the Comfort Package as standard. This includes Shift Assistant Pro for clutchless gear changes, heated grips, cruise control, Hill Start Control and adaptive headlight functionality through Headlight Pro. BMW is importing the R 12 G/S to India as a completely built-up unit, with deliveries commencing immediately. The motorcycle also comes with a 3-year/unlimited-kilometre warranty that can be extended into the fourth and fifth years.

title: ESPN’s Jimmy Pitaro on the New Playbook for Sports Fans - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Analysis and forecasts on global economies and markets for the year ahead from economists and strategists across Goldman Sachs. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The launch of ESPN’s direct-to-consumer service a year ago was a marker of change in the sports media business—offering the full suite of ESPN networks without a pay-TV bundle for the first time. ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro joins Dave Dase, global co-head of the Sports franchise in Investment Banking, and discusses how this challenging decision helps the company reach younger viewers and “serve the sports fan anytime, anywhere.” Pitaro also talks about the strength of ESPN’s current sports rights portfolio, why the company is sometimes willing to walk away from media rights negotiations, and explains how AI allows ESPN to create new offerings. Jimmy Pitaro:     The foundation of ESPN is live events. Everything that we do, original content, our 30 for 30, E60, SC Featured, our studio programming. It all is built off of that foundation of live games. Dave Dase:   Good afternoon. Welcome to Talks at GS. I'm Dave Dase. I head up our Southeast business and co-head our global sports business in investment banking. I'm joined today by Jimmy Pitaro, chairman of ESPN, who's led one of the most important transitions in sports media. Under Jimmy's leadership, ESPN launched its full direct-to-consumer streaming service, expanded its partnership with the NFL, and continued reshaping how fans watch, follow, and engage with sports, all of which we will discuss today. Jimmy, you signed and closed a deal with the NFL on Red Zone NFL Network earlier this year. Maybe just talk about the impact that's having, right, as you think about broadly NFL football. Jimmy Pitaro:     Well, let me first say thank you for the partnership on that. You were involved in that in that deal. We feel great about it. For those of you that don't know really what we're talking about, we acquired the NFL Network. ESPN did. We also acquired their entire fantasy business. We acquired their Red Zone linear business, and we acquired the Red Zone brand. In exchange, the league took a 10% equity stake in ESPN. Walt Disney Company owns the majority. We have another shareholder, Hearst. And now we have the NFL at 10%. The relationship with the league, I think, has never been better. I think they're very pleased with the deal. We're very pleased with the deal. We've now ingested NFL Network into the ESPN app, which I'm sure you want to talk about. But now if you're a subscriber to our premium tier called ESPN Unlimited, you have access to all the programming of NFL Network. We are, as I said before, the official game, the official fantasy game of the NFL. So, we've combined those two products. Many of you probably saw this. We had a US Open Red Zone, which filled me with joy. It was exactly what I was envisioning when we were negotiating this deal with the league and looking to acquire that Red Zone brand. Not just the linear product, but the Red Zone brand. What else could we do with that brand? We kicked it off with the US Open. We're looking at other opportunities. Potentially college football, although we haven't decided on that yet. That's something that's on the board. But we're in really good shape here with this deal. And we're excited about what it means for the future at ESPN. Dave Dase:   Maybe talk about a year ago you launched the direct-to-consumer platform and streaming platform. That was a tough decision. Something that was talked about in, you know, the ecosystem for many, many years, for you as well as other, certainly the other more traditional or legacy broadcast cable-oriented type businesses. But talk a little bit about that process, what your goals and objectives were, and just how it's performed thus far. Jimmy Pitaro:     You nailed it. It was a really tough decision. And the entire industry was focused on it. What is this going to mean? If ESPN goes direct-to-consumer over the top, what is that going to mean for cord cutting? Are all sports fans then going to cancel their paid TV subscription? We knew that wouldn't happen. I mean, we have, call it high-level, maybe one-third of the market from a sports viewership perspective. We don't have everything. We can't have everything. It doesn't work for us. From our perspective, knowing that it wasn't going to cause a total collapse of paid television, which has been very good to ESPN and the Walt Disney Company. It's a fantastic business model for us. We had to be very careful in terms of when we were going to actually go direct-to-consumer. And I spent many, many hours in a conference room with Bob Iger on this topic. And so, ultimately, we made the call that we would go summer of 2025. And so, we did it in August of last year. So, we just celebrated our one-year anniversary. Look, our strategy was what I often refer to as parallel paths. Meaning how do we make ourselves available to people who are not interested in paid television? Okay? Mostly the younger generation, but there are others my age that are just not interested in paid television anymore. We need to be there. Our mission is to serve the sports fan anytime, anywhere. And so, if you're not interested in paid television, we still need ESPN to be accessible to you. Okay, so we're going to go direct-to-consumer. At the same time, as I said before, paid television has been really important to us in our bottom line. And so, how do we go direct-to-consumer and protect that legacy or traditional business? And so, what we ended up doing, and this was a very challenging decision and somewhat of a polarizing topic early on in the discussions, we decided to make ESPN DTC available to all paid TV subscribers long-term. Ultimately, now we have to get the deals done with the distributors, but the vast majority of distributors today are now offering what we call entitlements. Meaning, if you're a subscriber to Charter, Comcast, YouTube TV, Hulu Live. You fire up the ESPN app. You enter your credentials and you get access to everything ESPN direct-to-consumer. So, what does that mean? That was our way of adding value to paid TV. So, we went direct-to-consumer. We're available there as an option. But if you're a paid TV subscriber, that subscription is far more valuable to you than it was yesterday. Two things. Timing. We knew we were going to go direct-to-consumer. It was a matter of when, not if. And do we offer these entitlements to paid TV subscribers? And the answer to that one was yes. Dave Dase:   Great. Let's talk a little bit about media rights. From my sense, the comprehensive best content out there, you probably have the strongest portfolio today as you've ever had. How do you think about the value proposition of what rights do you want? How do you think of return on investment? Jimmy Pitaro:     I get this question all the time. It's probably where I spend the most amount of time dealing with rights. The foundation of ESPN is live events. Everything that we do, original content, our 30 for 30, E60, SC Featured, our studio programming. It all is built off of that foundation of live games. And so, thank you for acknowledging that. Yes, our rights portfolio today, we're 47 years old at ESPN. And it's the best it's ever been. It's the best that the industry has ever seen from any one enterprise. So, we feel really good about that. At the same time, as I mentioned before, we cannot have everything. It just would not work for us financially. We spend just as much time analyzing things that we end up passing on as things that we end up acquiring. But we sit down, we do the analysis. We have a very sophisticated rights acquisitions team, a very sophisticated strategy team, finance team. We all get together. We look at value to pay television. Are the affiliates interested in this content? We look at projected ratings and corresponding ad sales. And then we look at value on the direct-to-consumer side. And then we make the best offer that we can. But we're at peace. If the league or the conference is looking for something significantly more, we're at peace with walking away. All that said, Dave, I still really like our hand. Historically, we're competing against NBC, CBS, and Fox. Today, we're still competing against the incumbents. And yet we're competing against Netflix, YouTube, Amazon, Apple, DAZN. And so, it's fiercely competitive. But I said I like our hand. And the reason why I said that is because we're the Walt Disney Company. And so, when we sit down at the table, we don't just bring ESPN linear. We bring everything that I mentioned before digitally. We bring broadcast through ABC. We bring Hulu. We bring Disney Plus. We bring the power of the theme parks for promotion. And so, I'm not quite sure a league or a conference is going to get that kind of value. We also bring the megaphone that is ESPN. We're the only folks that are covering sports every day, all day long, 365. We are in a really good place here because that portfolio that you mentioned, it's locked up. Like, for the next, I don't know, five to 10 years, we're in really good shape because those rights are spoken for now. Dave Dase:   Yeah. It seems like you have an interesting rights decision to make with respect to the college football playoff. Maybe talk about there's been an explosion in terms of sports valuations. We've certainly seen that. Women's sports, people are really talking about. There's real capital going into. And I often get asked the question by clients or investors or people who may want to buy a team, you know, what's going on? Why is this different now with women's sports? I give you and ESPN a lot of credit for - women's sports needed oxygen. And you, in some ways, were the oxygen, which gave distribution platform both at the college level as well as at the professional level. But talking about that. Was that intentional? Was it part of the strategy? How did you think about women's sports and how are you thinking about it today? Because it's a fantastic moment for, you know, both of us have daughters. And many of you, right, you have daughters who are playing sports and everything else. It's a fantastic time. Jimmy Pitaro:     Thank you for recognizing that. I can take zero credit for ESPN's investment in women's sports. It long predates me. This has been a multi-decade priority at the company. I mean, we were the WNBA launch partner 30 years ago. We've had the NCAA women's tournament for decades, which is a crown jewel in our portfolio. But I will tell you that, you know, over the past decade, we have significantly increased our investment in women's sports, both professional and college. You know, we now have a fantastic partnership with the NWSL. We have a partnership with Athletes Unlimited on the softball side, which we love. That's another sport that's on fire. Women's volleyball is on fire. Everything volleyball is up and to the right. We're also, as an extension of the live games, we're investing in women's fantasy. Fantasy is a big part of our DNA at ESPN. We have significantly more women's studio programming today than we did a decade ago. We love the fact that the industry is kind of working with us here. It's not just ESPN. Others are clearly-- our competitors are clearly making investments as well. And what we're seeing is this rising tide. And last thing I'd say on this is the dollars are following. Like advertisers, sponsors are very focused on women's sports. So, fandom is heading that way. And so are the dollars. So, it makes perfect sense for us on a variety of levels to be increasing our investments. Dave Dase:   Incredibly competitive, right, areas to be in, in and of themselves. What was your approach? For a sports fan out there, they would say, gosh, you have the dream job, right? Running ESPN. But what was your approach just from a career development kind of advice? Or how did you get to where you got to? Or, you know, what sort of skill set got you there? Jimmy Pitaro:     Well, I am, as you are, I'm a crazy sports fan. My wife thinks I need therapy on this. Like, I'm not exaggerating when I say my mood is completely dependent on how the Yankees do like the next day and how Notre Dame football does. My whole life has been team sports. Dave and I also played together. And so, I know you can relate to this, but my whole life, I've just loved team sports. By the way, this started at Edgemont High School in Scarsdale, New York, which is where your CEO went. David's younger brother was my classmate at Edgemont High School. And he was a friend of mine. But my fandom, my crazy fandom, I was surrounded by crazy sports fans. My mom does not watch it when the Yankees are in the field because she thinks nothing good can happen when the Yankees are in the field. Like that's how crazy-- My sister is the general counsel of Major League Baseball. Like I'm surrounded by crazy sports-- all of my friends, we used to leave Edgemont High School and go to the Bronx and sit in the bleachers. So, my crazy fandom started then. You know, played in college. And you know, my fandom just continued to grow. I was a lawyer. I learned a ton. I went to law school and practiced. I was a litigator for several years. Learned a ton on the litigation side, really starting with like public speaking and the importance of brevity. But yes, then I made the transition to the business side at Yahoo and got immersed in technology. That was a blessing for me. Everyone has breaks during their careers. And so, when I was asked to leave law and run a business, it was Yahoo Sports. I went from managing 12 people to managing over a thousand people overnight, most of whom were technicians, engineers, front end, back end engineers, designers. I'm this lawyer guy managing these folks. And that was quite daunting. But baptism by fire. I learned a ton. By the way, I was competing with ESPN every day of my life. I woke up every day and challenged the team, how are we going to beat ESPN? Anyway, I met Bob Iger, Steve Jobs, who I'd worked with, and Sheryl Sandberg, who I knew very well, were on the Disney board. They were looking to make a change. Bob was looking to make a change on the digital side. That's actually how I joined the Walt Disney Company, not to run ESPN, but to lead Disney Interactive, their digital horizontal business. It doesn't exist anymore today. But because of my Yahoo days and being immersed in technology, I was able to take a lot of that learning and be effective at Disney Interactive. And then in 2017, the gentleman who was running ESPN resigned. Working for Bob was such a blessing. Every year during my review with Bob, he would ask me, or we would have a conversation around what I wanted to do next and would always end with ESPN. So, fast forward to 2017, the ESPN job opens up and Bob calls me, "I'm assuming you want this?" I said, "Yes." And then I had to interview 16 times. I had an interview with the entire board and several people in corporate. Anyway, ended up getting the job. And it's been a dream. Dave Dase:   Talk a little bit about your management style today, sitting on top of this organization all over the world, 24-7, 365. You have massive personalities, right, in the media business. You have best-in-class innovative technology. What's your management style? How do you handle this? Jimmy Pitaro:     I just love being a part of a team. I really do. And so, the highlight of my week is my senior staff meeting. All of my direct reports and I get together, and we sit in our ESPN boardroom, and I say, "Discuss, debate, decide a line." And so, our chief of staff puts together the agenda. And we have real tough debates. She'll tee up the discussion and we will debate. And my direct reports know that not only can they challenge me, but I'm still learning. Every single day, I'm trying to learn and be an effective leader, but I want to be, I need to be challenged. I don't just want yes people around me. We have really healthy discussion and debate. And then we try to decide as a team. We don't get paralyzed by the analysis. We try to decide as a team. And more often than not, far more often than not, we do. But there are times where we can't agree. And so, then I make the decision. That's what I'm getting paid to do. And then the most important part of that is alignment, right? Once the decision is made, and I feel really strongly about this, and I've had some roadblocks in my career on this last one, but as a leader at the Walt Disney Company and ESPN, you lose the luxury of questioning the decision after it's been made. Right? You want a forum to be heard. And you have that at ESPN. But once we make the decision, or I make the decision, then the expectation is alignment, even if you were in the minority, you didn't agree with the decision. You asked me what my leadership philosophy is. There are several components to that. But at a macro level, I think that's the most important thing I would call out. Dave Dase:   We talked a little bit about artificial intelligence. As you sit here today, as we sit here today, what do you think it's like being a fan 10 years from now, 20 years from now? Where does this innovation go? I had this debate with some team owners around, is there ultimately a physical sporting world and, you know, a completely digital, in essence, sporting world that coexists, overlapped to some extent? But just with AI and everything else, where do you think this goes? And I will say, right, most of the owners who are calling, or most people who want to deploy capital - institutions, individuals, billionaires who want to deploy capital into sports teams, are now, at least for the last 9 or 12 months, saying it's a hedge on AI. Right? Dave Dase:   People want to be there. It's a true hedge. It's an asset allocation play. And I think, in large part, I mean, we've seen some pretty significant uptick in sports valuations. And so, I think part of that, you know, is from that. But just how do you think about AI and where does this go and what's it like to be a fan? Jimmy Pitaro:     My old boss contributed to that increase. Dave Dase:   He did. He did, yes. Teams are being bought, not sold. Jimmy Pitaro:     Yeah. Everyone's talking about AI today, of course. We've been invested in AI for many, many years at ESPN. And so, the SportsCenter For You that I mentioned before would not exist without AI. But for us, AI has been nothing but a blessing. And for the sports fan, from my perspective, it's been nothing but a blessing. It hasn't displaced jobs. Okay? If anything, it's helping our business grow so that we can hire more people. Like, that's how I look at it. But examples outside of SportsCenter For You? Highlights. Highlight generation. Like, a lot of that is being generated through AI. We can generate far more highlights at scale than we ever could before. We talked about women's sports, but some of the smaller leagues, like the Premier Lacrosse League, NWSL, TGL, we can now do game recaps that are automatically generated. Now, we can't go out and hire 5,000 people to create game recaps. It just would not be cost effective for us. We're running a business. But now, through AI, and it's not always perfect, but we can generate game recaps. Investigative reporting. I talk about this all the time. My commute to Bristol, Connecticut, sometimes I'm in the car for an hour and a half. And so, our investigative reports oftentimes could take you 30, 45 minutes to read. They're very lengthy and in-depth. And I don't have the time to get through all of that. So, now, you can just tap on the Listen button and the narration is automatically generated. I expect to see a lot more of that. In terms of your point on sports being somewhat AI-proof, I do agree with that for the most part. Again, full circle, I think AI is going to do nothing but-- not just for ESPN, but for the industry, is going to improve the experience. Whether it's in stadium - we all know what's happening now with places like Cosm. Like, that whole experience is off the charts great from my perspective. And I think that's just going to continue to improve. Dave Dase:   Well, thank you very much. Thanks for being a client. Thanks for being so generous with your time. Most importantly, thanks for providing all this content that makes everybody's lives so interesting. Jimmy Pitaro:     Thank you for having me, everybody. Appreciate it. Ontario Provincial Police have charged two people after seizing more than $850,000 of illegal cannabis and dismantling a commercial-scale size grow-op near Belleville. In October, the OPP Joint Forces Cannabis Enforcement Team (PJFCET) began an investigation into a suspected illegal cannabis production site in Tyendinaga Township, 10 kilometres east of Belleville, after being tipped off by a member of the public. On Oct. 29, members of the OPP’s PJFCET and Emergency Response Team, as well as Lennox and Addington County OPP, executed a search warrant at the property and made two arrests. As a result of the investigation, 900 illegal cannabis plants, 190 kilograms of illegal cannabis, 215 kilograms of illegal cannabis shake, 125 illegal cannabis clones, and three cellphones were seized. The total estimated street value of the illegal cannabis is $850,000, police said in a news release Wednesday. Quoc Ly, 58, and Qi Sen Zhang, 64, both of Tyendinaga Township, have both been charged with possession of illicit cannabis for the purpose of distribution and cultivate illicit cannabis. The accused were released from custody and are scheduled to appear before the Ontario Court of Justice in Napanee on Jan. 26. Back in September, the OPP seized nearly $3 million in illicit cannabis on Tyendinaga Mohawk Territory and charged eight men.
