title: NBA Power Rankings: One wild stat for all 30 teams - ESPN
content:
The first month of the 2026-2027 NBA season is in the books! In the surprisingly deep West, the San Antonio Spurs continue to pace the conference, with a point differential of plus-11.2. The next four teams in the West -- the Minnesota Timberwolves, Memphis Grizzlies, Houston Rockets and Los Angeles Lakers -- would all rank No. 2 in the East. Speaking of the East, the Boston Celtics continue to surge, outscoring opponents by an average of 11.5 points per game, while the Philadelphia 76ers, despite a 12-3 record, have beaten teams by just 2.8 points per game. The Detroit Pistons, last year's No. 1 seed, continue to sputter, while the 2026 champion New York Knicks are 8-6 -- sixth in a wide-open conference. In this week's Power Rankings, our insiders rank each of the 30 teams and also highlight one illuminating statistic per team to watch over the coming months. Previous rankings: Preseason | Oct. 28 | Nov. 4 | Nov. 11 Jump to a team:
ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE
DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND
LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN
NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX
POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS Next games: vs. LAC (Nov. 19), vs. NO (Nov. 21), @ SAC (Nov. 23) That's how many wins in a row the Spurs piled up after losing two in a row to start the season. The last time San Antonio pieced together a 10-game winning streak before the month of December was November 2013, the same season the Spurs captured their fifth NBA championship. What's more, San Antonio ran off the winning streak playing with an experimental three-guard lineup that the Spurs committed to implementing over the summer. So far, the lineup is working, demonstrating great roster and on-court versatility for San Antonio as its operation evolves around Victor Wembanyama. -- Michael C. Wright Next games: vs. UTAH (Nov. 18), vs. SAC (Nov. 20), vs. UTAH (Nov. 23) That's Luka Doncic's point total so far this season, the third most in NBA history through the first 13 games of a season, trailing only Wilt Chamberlain. Doncic is averaging 39.0 points per game, which would be the third-highest scoring average for a season if he keeps it up, with only Chamberlain ahead of him in the top two spots. -- Dave McMenamin Next games: @ DEN (Nov. 18), @ SAC (Nov. 21), @ GS (Nov. 22), @ WAS (Nov. 24) Boston is allowing 99.7 points per game on the road, the only team in the league under 100 and almost four points fewer than the next-closest team, the Charlotte Hornets (103.8). The Celtics were the league's fourth-best defense last season but allowed 107.3 points per game on the road in the regular season, which was still the best in the league. If they hold to this stout defensive start, they'd be the first team to hold road opponents to under 100 points per game since the San Antonio Spurs and Utah Jazz did it in the 2016-17 season. -- Kris Rhim Next games: @ ORL (Nov. 18), vs. MIL (Nov. 21), vs. POR (Nov. 23) The Sixers have the best record in the Eastern Conference and their second-best start in the past 40 seasons. But they've jumped out to that start without exactly dominating their opponents, with just a 2.8-point average differential, ranking 11th in the NBA. According to ESPN's BPI, the Sixers have an expected win percentage of 60.1%, which is significantly lower than their actual 80% winning percentage. Sixers guard VJ Edgecombe acknowledged this point following a win over the Nets: "We haven't had ... a dominant win yet that we know we're capable of." -- Rhim Next games: @ IND (Nov. 18), @ DEN (Nov. 20), vs. LAC (Nov. 23) That's where the Houston Rockets rank in the NBA in assist-to-turnover ratio after finishing No. 27 last season, which played a major role in the Rockets posting a 22-23 record last season in clutch-time games. The return of veteran point guard Fred VanVleet is driving Houston's improvement, and the numbers will be even better when the 32-year-old is able to play the second night of back-to-backs as he recovers from last year's ACL surgery. -- Wright Next games: vs. NYK (Nov. 19), vs. MEM (Nov. 21), vs. BKN (Nov. 23) No Anthony Edwards? No problem for the Timberwolves (at least not yet). Minnesota has posted a blistering plus-12.6 net rating when LaMelo Ball shares the court with Ayo Dosunmu, Edwards' replacement in the starting lineup. ESPN Analytics has unveiled its new NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web app for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades. Can you build the perfectly balanced trade that fans of all teams involved would accept?
• Build your own trades here
• More NBA coverage For comparison's sake, the Spurs hold the NBA's best overall net rating at ... wait for it ... plus-12.6. Dosunmu has picked a great time to shoot the lights out: The 2021 second-round pick is averaging a career-high 17.8 points per game on 52/43/91 splits. Timberwolves executive Tim Connelly should be charged with grand larceny for plucking Dosunmu from the Bulls before last season's trade deadline. -- Ben Golliver Next games: @ MIL (Nov. 19), @ NYK (Nov. 21), @ PHI (Nov. 23) Opposing teams are shooting just 32.1% on 3-pointers against Portland, the lowest mark in the NBA. The Blazers, who have made 56 more 3-pointers than they have allowed through 13 games, are outscoring opponents by an average of 12.9 points per game from beyond the arc. Given that Portland's offense also ranks among the league's best in generating free throw attempts, it's no surprise the Blazers have jumped up to sixth in offense after finishing 21st last season. -- Golliver Next games: @ NO (Nov. 18), vs. TOR (Nov. 20), @ ATL (Nov. 22), @ ORL (Nov. 24) Rebounds averaged by small forward Ausar Thompson. The fourth-year vet has been asked to contribute more on the glass and as a playmaker, but because of the absence of center Jalen Duren, Thompson's dramatic increase on the boards has been critical in keeping the Pistons afloat. The 6-foot-7 Thompson ranks 18th in the league in rebounding. Grizzlies wing Cedric Coward is the only other swingman who ranks in the top 55. Thompson has become more of an offensive initiator, too, as J.B. Bickerstaff works to lessen the load of Cade Cunningham. While it has been a work in progress, sometimes stifling Thompson's athleticism, he is still averaging more than five assists per game to start the season. And with the recent injury to Duncan Robinson, Thompson will add even more responsibility on offense to keep Detroit within striking distance in the East. -- Vince Goodwill Next games: vs. ATL (Nov. 18), vs. NO (Nov. 20), @ MIA (Nov. 22), @ IND (Nov. 23) Oklahoma City's offense produces 118.0 points per 100 possessions with back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on the floor -- and only 100.0 when he sits. It stands to reason that the offense won't be as efficient without one of the league's elite scorers, but the drop-off is much more significant than it has been in the past few seasons. The hope is that Ajay Mitchell will continue to improve as he gets more reps as the primary initiator in non-SGA lineups. -- Tim MacMahon Next games: vs. BOS (Nov. 18), vs. HOU (Nov. 20), @ CHI (Nov. 22), vs. DAL (Nov. 24) Jamal Murray has made 41 of his 87 attempted 3s through 12 games. Among players who have attempted at least 50 3s, that 47.1% accuracy rate is the best in the NBA. Murray has been scorching hot. He's shooting 51% overall from the field and 86% from the line, averaging a career-high 26.1 points. Nuggets coach David Adelman said recently that he believes Murray is performing like one of the best players in the world and it would be discussed more if Denver had won a few more games. The Nuggets are a reasonable but unspectacular 7-5, thriving with Murray on the floor (plus-59) but drowning when he sits (minus-51). -- Anthony Slater Next games: @ CLE (Nov. 18), vs. GS (Nov. 19), @ MIN (Nov. 21), @ CHA (Nov. 23) That's Memphis' road record this season. The Grizzlies have won seven in a row on the road, which ties a franchise record for the most consecutive road wins at any point of a season (they won seven straight in 2010). Memphis has a chance to break the record Wednesday at Cleveland. Ty Jerome leads the way for the Grizzlies, averaging a career-high 25.4 points, and he is flanked by a pair of young players on the rise in Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward. Boozer ranks as the third player since the merger to rack up at least 200 points, 100 rebounds and 75 assists through 14 career games, joining Ben Simmons (2017-18) and Magic Johnson (1979-80). -- Wright Next games: @ MIN (Nov. 19), vs. POR (Nov. 21), vs. IND (Nov. 22) That's the combined 3-point shooting percentage for OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart, a big part of why the Knicks have a 15th-ranked offense. Last year, the Knicks used Mike Brown's "let it fly" ethos to rise to the top three in that category before their improbable playoff run. Landry Shamet and Miles McBride are valuable reserves, shooting well over 40%, keeping the Knicks slightly above league average. Shamet, in many instances, has finished games ahead of Bridges. McBride's 43.5 clip represents a career high and it would help if he got more opportunities, especially as the starters ease their way into the second month of the season. -- Goodwill We knew the addition of Giannis Antetokounmpo would eventually provide a jolt to the Heat's offense. And after a slow start, Miami now ranks ninth in offense and leads the Eastern Conference in points per game (119.4), trailing only the Los Angeles Lakers and Memphis Grizzlies overall. Over their recent five-game winning streak, Miami has been ever better, averaging 125.4 PPG and shooting 36.4% on 3-pointers. A key to the Heat's success on offense is lack of turnovers. In their past five games, Miami ranks first in the league in assist-to-turnover ratio and has allowed the fewest points off turnovers. -- Bobby Marks Next games: @ OKC (Nov. 18), vs. CHA (Nov. 20), vs. DET (Nov. 22) Slow starts are typical for the Hawks. In their past four games, Atlanta has been outscored by 11.8 points in the first quarter. Those four games have seen opponents average 34.5 PPG in the first quarter. Defensively, in these first frames, Atlanta has allowed opponents to shoot 59.6% from the field and 45.7% on 3-pointers. Overall, Atlanta trails only Golden State for the worst plus-minus (minus-4.9) in the first quarter of games. -- Marks Next games: @ DAL (Nov. 18), @ MEM (Nov. 19), vs. BOS (Nov. 22) In Stephen Curry's 263 minutes this season, the Warriors have a 118.6 offensive rating. That's equivalent to a top-five NBA offense and, during Curry's 10 games, was enough to lift them to a 7-3 record. "The Hoop Collective" podcast, hosted by Brian Windhorst, releases new shows every Monday, Wednesday and Friday during the NBA season.
• Listen to the latest episodes But with Curry sidelined with a torn oblique, the Warriors' lack of scoring punch through the rest of the roster has been exposed. In Curry's 414 minutes on the bench this season, the Warriors have an offensive rating of 109.4, which would currently land sixth worst among the 30 teams. They've been pummeled 38-14 and 35-11 the last two first quarters without him, coming out so sluggishly offensively that coach Steve Kerr declared the need to rearrange lineup combinations in search of something that works better. -- Slater Next games: vs. MEM (Nov. 18), vs. IND (Nov. 20), @ CHI (Nov. 23) At age 37 and in his 18th year in the league, the mileage looks like its starting to pile up on James Harden. His numbers are down across the board -- scoring, assists and overall field goal percentage -- but nowhere is that trend more glaring than Harden's shooting percentage on 2-pointers. Entering Tuesday, that number sat at a career-worst 40.2% inside the arc, down significantly from last season's 49.5%. The Cavs are going to need Harden to bounce back as a threat going toward the basket or consistently finish at the rim if he's going to continue orchestrating their offense as Donovan Mitchell's co-star. -- Jamal Collier Next games: vs. GS (Nov. 18), vs. LAC (Nov. 21), @ UTAH (Nov. 22), @ DEN (Nov. 24) The Mavericks need to figure out how to pack their game when they travel. Dallas has been one of the league's worst road teams, going 2-5 with a minus-12.6 net rating away from the American Airlines Center. The Mavs just completed one of the worst road trips in recent memory, losing by 39 points in Minnesota, 10 in Cleveland (despite the Cavaliers sitting their entire starting lineup) and 37 in Boston. -- MacMahon Next games: vs. WAS (Nov. 18), @ DET (Nov. 20), vs. MIL (Nov. 23) The Raptors got off to a dominant defensive start to begin this season, forcing 24 turnovers through the first three games. But they have cooled off since, forcing just 16 turnovers over their last six. Still, the Raptors lead the league in turnover percentage at 16.8%. Toronto's turnover prowess could shift again quickly, though, whenever Kawhi Leonard returns from the left knee soreness that has kept him out of all but two games this season. -- Rhim Next games: vs. PHI (Nov. 18), @ BKN (Nov. 20), @ WAS (Nov. 22), vs. DET (Nov. 24) We are seeing the impact of new head coach Sean Sweeney over the past 10 days. After starting the season 2-7, Orlando has won four straight games, the turnaround spurred by a fourth-ranked defense. During the four-game winning streak, the Magic have allowed the second-fewest fast-break points and fifth-fewest second-chance points. While three of its wins were against teams at the bottom of the standings (Sacramento, Utah, Milwaukee), Orlando had its signature victory of the season at Boston on Monday. In the win, the Magic held the Celtics to their third-fewest points this season (105). -- Marks Next games: @ SAC (Nov. 18), @ UTAH (Nov. 20), @ NO (Nov. 23) While the analytical movement in the NBA has prioritized 3-pointers, free throws and shots at the rim, the midrange shot is alive and well in Phoenix. The Suns are generating 9.0% of their points per game in the midrange, which ranks fifth in the NBA. A lot of this has to do with five-time All-Star Devin Booker's preferred style of play. Phoenix also ranks No. 2 in the league in points per game off pull-up jump shots (28.7 PPG). -- McMenamin Next games: vs. HOU (Nov. 18), @ CLE (Nov. 20), @ NYK (Nov. 22), vs. OKC (Nov. 23) Indiana has looked lost without its star point guard, Tyrese Haliburton, for two years now. He has played in four games this season, and though the Pacers are just 2-2 during those contests, they are five points per 100 possessions better on offense (and 4.5 points better on defense) with Haliburton on the court. Coach Rick Carlisle said during his radio appearance this week that there is still no definitive timeline for Haliburton's return. Next games: @ SA (Nov. 19), @ DAL (Nov. 21), @ HOU (Nov. 23) The Clippers are shooting 39.1% on 3-pointers this season, which ranks second in the league. While LA's offense ranks 21st overall, coach Tyronn Lue has found success spreading the floor with Derrick Jones Jr. and Gradey Dick both shooting above 50% from deep; Brook Lopez and Kris Dunn both shooting above 40%; and Keaton Wagler and Darius Garland both hovering in the high 30s. The team has been particularly effective at shooting corner 3s, hitting 41.6% combined from either side of the court. -- McMenamin Next games: @ TOR (Nov. 18), @ CHI (Nov. 20), vs. ORL (Nov. 22), vs. BOS (Nov. 24) Trae Young is on pace to have the worst season of his career. Outside of last season, when he played just 15 games as he battled injuries, Young is averaging career lows in points (17.9), field goal percentage (37.8%) and 3-point percentage (30.6%). Young is also attempting just 13 field goals per game, a career low. The four-time All-Star signed a four-year, $212 million contract extension in July. -- Rhim Wednesday, Nov. 25
• Heat-76ers, 5 p.m. ET
• Timberwolves-Thunder 7:30 p.m. ET
• Spurs-Trail Blazers, 10 p.m. ET With LaMelo Ball traded to Minnesota, Kon Knueppel sidelined by a hamstring injury and Brandon Miller struggling, the Hornets have the NBA's worst offense (102.5 points per 100 possessions). That mark is down nearly 16 points from last season, when they ranked fifth. The last time the NBA saw an offense as anemic as Charlotte's was the 2015-16 season, back when Golden State star Stephen Curry was launching the 3-point revolution. The Hornets have come by their terrible offense honestly: They rank 29th in 3-point percentage and dead last in 2-point percentage, free throw attempts, turnovers and assists. -- Golliver Next games: vs. DET (Nov. 18), @ OKC (Nov. 20), @ SA (Nov. 21), vs. PHX (Nov. 23) The Pelicans shouldn't lose any sleep over Dejounte Murray's trade request. The veteran guard has posted a terrible minus-12.8 NET rating this season. New Orleans, which went 1-8 with Murray in the lineup, has gone 4-2 without him, thanks to a blowout win over the Warriors on Monday. While the tension between Murray and the organization is a reminder that the front office sat on its hands during the offseason, the saga should create more opportunities for 2025 lottery pick Jeremiah Fears. -- Golliver Next games: vs. CHI (Nov. 18), vs. ORL (Nov. 20), @ MIN (Nov. 23) Nolan Traore looks like the best player from the Nets' 2025 draft class, having scored in double figures in seven straight games. His longest such streak last season was four. Outside of Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr., offense is hard to come by for these Nets, but Traore is averaging nearly 17 points per game this month on 54% shooting and 46% from 3-point range. He has leapfrogged rookie teammate Mikel Brown Jr. as far as reliability and will be given ample room to grow. -- Goodwill Next games: @ BKN (Nov. 18), vs. WAS (Nov. 20), vs. DEN (Nov. 22), vs. CLE (Nov. 23) The central figures on this Bulls roster -- Caleb Wilson, Matas Buzelis and even veteran Norman Powell -- are best served finishing plays instead of starting them, which makes Josh Giddey's role as a playmaker even more important for this offense. However, Giddey's turnover percentage this season has skyrocketed to 24.9%, the highest mark in his career, while his 4.2 turnovers per 36 minutes are the fifth highest in the league. -- Collier Next games: @ MIA (Nov. 18), vs. POR (Nov. 19), @ PHI (Nov. 21), @ TOR (Nov. 23) The Bucks are 1-13 and have lost 10 straight games -- the franchise's worst start in 52 years (the team dropped 13 of its first 14 games in 1974 when Kareem Abdul-Jabbar got injured). The franchise record for losses in a row is 15, which belongs to the 1995-96 Milwaukee squad. The Bucks are in Miami on Wednesday for their first matchup against Giannis Antetokounmpo, who no-sold the meeting as "just another game." Perhaps it's because there aren't many of these Bucks whom Antetokounmpo recognizes. -- Collier Next games: @ LAL (Nov. 18), vs. PHX (Nov. 20), vs. DAL (Nov. 22), @ LAL (Nov. 23) There aren't a lot of pretty statistics for the Jazz, who lost 12 in a row before Tuesday night's win over the Clippers. Utah's offensive numbers are especially ugly: The team has posted a 105.1 offensive rating and a 50.8 effective field goal percentage, both of which rank second to last in the league. Utah's entire starting frontcourt is sidelined by injuries. Rookie guard Darryn Peterson's recent performance has been a bright spot, as the No. 2 pick has averaged 23.2 points on a respectable 54.1% eFG in his last six games. -- MacMahon Next games: vs. PHX (Nov. 18), @ LAL (Nov. 20), vs. BOS (Nov. 21), vs. SA (Nov. 23) There are countless early-season stats that spell out the Kings' bleak situation: 27th in offense, 29th in defense, the only team without a win at home yet. But how about this one? Rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. is tied for the NBA lead in minutes per game at 36.8. The last rookie to top that category for a full season was Wilt Chamberlain in 1960. So at least the Kings are giving an ocean of opportunity, shot attempts and development time to the most important player on their roster. It hasn't been flawless, but Acuff is flashing statistically: 25.5 points and 7.1 assists per game. -- Slater
